applicationPool.reason: the only pool entry that is simultaneously a real React Native application with a checked-in root ios/ project, reachable with no account and no hosted service, and buildable for the simulator without a signing identity. Containment is required on four points: the app target embeds a watch app, a widgets extension and a stickers extension, which must be stripped from the campaign scheme; ios/BlueWallet/BlueWallet.entitlements requests aps-environment, an application group and the camera, which are inert only because an unsigned simulator build embeds no entitlements; older revisions hardcode DEVELOPMENT_TEAM = A7W54YZ4WU in four build configurations, so the build recipe must force it empty rather than assume it is unset; and Electrum network access must be blocked, which restricts selection to defects whose trigger is local

selectedDefects.whySuitable: the trigger is Tools, then is it my address, typing an all-caps bech32 address into a React Native TextInput and pressing check. Text entered through XCUITest travels native keyboard to RCTUITextField to the Hermes side through onChangeText, is normalized by the wallet-matching logic there, and the result is rendered back into a native text view. That is exactly the react-native-ios adapter's full loop: the iOS text input surface plus the JS engine, and the defect is a casing normalization bug, so the precise bytes crossing the bridge decide the outcome. Fully offline: address matching is local

simulatorBuildWithoutSigning.evidence: built at both revisions under a build root with no symlink component. CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO is not what works: DEVELOPMENT_TEAM must be forced empty and CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY set to the ad-hoc identity, which keeps the aps-environment and application-group entitlements in the product and avoids the launch SIGTRAP the SwiftUI work first hit

selectedDefects.whySuitable: the strongest adapter-level candidate in this set. On the affected revision the row padding sits on the outer wrapper view rather than on the pressable, so the padded band around a note title is drawn but is not part of the hit area: a tap landing there is swallowed and the note does not open. The fix moves paddingLeft, paddingRight, paddingTop and paddingBottom onto the pressable. Nothing about this is visible to a JavaScript-only harness, because the styles are identical and only the native view that receives the touch differs; it can be seen only by sending a real coordinate tap through XCUITest into the RN view hierarchy and then asking the accessibility tree whether the note screen was pushed. That is precisely what the react-native-ios adapter owns. Entirely offline and needs no account
remaining: build the affected and fixed revisions for the simulator with CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO and a scheme that excludes ShareExtension, and record the exact command and result
state how the harness computes the padding coordinate from the row's accessibility frame, since a centre tap opens the note on both revisions and would not separate them
state the exact identity and authority for the observable, and minimize the trigger
run three affected reproductions and three fixed controls on a reset simulator with reset evidence
record neighboring legal behavior: a tap on the note title itself must still open the note on the affected build
selectedDefects.executionOutcome: complete campaign. Three affected reproductions all landing on react-native-layout:note-row-padding-outside-touch-target, three fixed controls all opening the note from the identical coordinate, neighbouring legal behaviour holding on both revisions, a corpus of one clean and two adversarial subjects with zero false positives, and the owned simulator deleted. The note row is an XCUIElementTypeButton whose frame is the pressable the fix changes: 370 by 20 affected, 402 by 52 fixed, both centred at (201, 137), so one absolute tap at (201, 118) is a fair trigger for both
